title: Does asking communities to contribute to development projects improve impact and cost-effectiveness?
summary: A field experiment in Bangladesh finds that requiring cash contributions for safe drinking-water wells sharply reduces take-up and impact, whereas labour contributions work about as well as no contribution at all – yet either requirement leaves the programme less cost-effective.

title: Using mobile phones to support teachers, parents, and students
summary: A new J-PAL Policy Insight reviewing 30 studies across low- and middle-income countries finds that mobile phones can improve student learning, teacher performance, and parental engagement, but only when paired with interactive, two-way pedagogy rather than one-way messaging.

title: Should workers or managers decide who gets rewarded?
summary: A field experiment with Indian carpet firms finds that letting workers vote on rewards boosts attendance but enables collusion, while giving managers discretion boosts output but damages workplace cohesion.

title: Does private preschool really give children a head start?
summary: In rural India, children in private preschools learn far more than those in public ones. Unequal access to private preschools explains most of the learning gap between richer and poorer children at school entry.

title: Can a one-hour documentary change long-term economic behaviour?
summary: A randomised trial in rural Ethiopia found that a single one-hour screening of documentaries featuring relatable role models produced lasting increases in farm investment, schooling, and household wealth five years on.

title: Rethinking multiple hypothesis testing: A welfare-based approach

title: How AI can put 20 years of development evidence to work
summary: A new playbook from J-PAL argues that AI's value in development lies not in the technology itself but in how well it is grafted onto decades of existing evidence about what improves lives.

title: Can bank access help farmers weather climate shocks?
summary: India's 1980s rural bank branch expansion only had modest effects on average agricultural output, but it substantially reduced farmers' vulnerability to adverse rainfall shocks, largely by helping them sustain irrigation.

title: The birth of Bangladesh: How the Bhola cyclone fostered revolution
summary: New research using satellite data on the 1970 Bhola cyclone shows that the storm's uneven intensity across East Pakistan increased support for the Awami League and recruitment of freedom fighters, helping tip the balance toward Bangladesh's independence.

title: Does making formality less costly actually pay off?
